 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Minnesota Wild ( 6-3-2 ) open a weekend back-to-back in Seattle on Saturday night, one day before Quinn Hughes plays in Vancouver for the first time since the Canucks traded their captain to Minnesota last December.
 That homecoming is not the only Hughes storyline hanging over this road trip. The 27-year-old is in the final season of a contract that carries a $7.85 million cap hit , and he is on track to become an unrestricted free agent next July.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement All this just hours after Olympic teammate Connor Hellebuyck was traded to New Jersey Friday, where Hughes' brothers Jack and Luke already play. As you can imagine, there's some anxiety creeping into the minds of MN Wild fans across the State of Hockey.
 Quinn Hughes hints at incoming contract extension with MN Wild?
 On Saturday, however, Joe Smith (The Athletic) tried to ask Quinn Hughes the same contract question he's been unwilling to answer so far. Is he going to re-sign in Minnesota or not? This time, though, the eldest Hughes brother had something very different to say.
 Instead of uncertainty, Quinn hinted for the first time at progress in contract talks with the Wild, telling Smith and other reporters gathered out in Seattle that his feet are "firmly planted" in Minnesota and that we shouldn't be surprised if "something happens soon."
 I asked Quinn Hughes about his contract situation, and he said his two feet are "firmly planted" in Minnesota. And he said he wouldn't be surprised if something happens "soon." #mnwild .
 — Joe Smith (@JoeSmithNHL) October 24, 2026 
 Related: How Connor Hellebuyck Trade Might Hurt/Help MN Wild 
 Quinn Hughes to reporters in Seattle on contract talks.
"I'm where I've always been. I'm excited right now. My two feet are planted in Minnesota and you know, something could happen soon. I'm not really to sure. I'm really enjoying playing here. I love playing with, you see
 — Dylan Loucks (@DylanLoucks4) October 24, 2026 
 That is a noticeably different tone from where things stood just yesterday. In Friday's piece on the Hellebuyck deal, Pierre LeBrun (The Athletic) wrote that Hughes "remains undecided on his future" after checking in again this week, and that he had not told the Wild whether he would extend or not.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Obviously, Hughes did not say anything about his deal being done, and the Wild have not announced anything. But it sure sounds like Quinn knows something that we don't and that's a step in the right direction.
 What Quinn Hughes has meant to the Minnesota Wild
 The Wild know exactly what they would be paying for, if Quinn signs on the dotted line for what is expected to be over $20 million per year. After the trade last season, Hughes put up 53 points (five goals, 48 assists) in 48 games for Minnesota while averaging 27:54 of ice time.
 He was even better in the playoffs, with 15 points (four goals, 11 assists) in 11 games and an average of 30:57 per night. Through 11 games this season, he has 13 points, including five on the power play, and he is logging 27:25 a night.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Hughes is also closing in on a milestone. He has 498 career points in 518 regular-season games , leaving him two away from 500 heading into Saturday's game in Seattle and Sunday's return to Vancouver.
